hook.en: A very light osteopathic method: hold a joint at the point where its ligaments feel evenly balanced, until the tissue seems to settle.
hook.ur: Balanced Ligamentous Tension (BLT) ek bohat gentle osteopathic approach hai jisme joint ko us position mein rakha jata hai jahan ligament tension barabar mehsoos ho.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Balanced Ligamentous Tension (BLT) is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (4 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Balanced Ligamentous Tension (BLT) kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 4 checks.)

text.en: Balanced Ligamentous Tension (BLT) is an osteopathic approach in which you hold a joint in the position where ligament tension feels equal in all directions. You wait for a sense of release. It is gentle and slow.
text.ur: BLT mein joint ko aisi position mein hold kiya jata hai jahan ligament tension mukhtalif directions mein barabar mehsoos ho. Practitioner phir tissue ke settle hone ka intezar karta hai. Approach slow aur gentle hoti hai.

simpler.en: A very light osteopathic method: hold a joint at the point where its ligaments feel evenly balanced, until the tissue seems to settle.
simpler.ur: Balanced Ligamentous Tension (BLT) ek bohat gentle osteopathic approach hai jisme joint ko us position mein rakha jata hai jahan ligament tension barabar mehsoos ho.

text.en: Like balancing a tent with guy ropes: you adjust until all ropes feel equally taut, then the tent sits still.
text.ur: Tension ropes wali tent ko balance karne jaisa: ropes ko adjust karte hain jab tak pull barabar na lage, phir tent stable hota hai. Yeh analogy hai, mechanism ka saboot nahi.

text.en:
Three ideas carry this whole technique:
**1.** Find the neutral point of balance rather than pushing a barrier.
**2.** Hold light contact and wait.
**3.** The perceived release is subjective, so judge results by patient-reported change.
text.ur: Barrier ko push karne ke bajaye balance ka neutral point dhoondhein, halkay contact ke sath wait karein, aur result ko patient-reported change se judge karein. Point of balance woh position hai jahan tissue tension barabar mehsoos ho. Ligamentous tension ligament ka pull hai; release practitioner ka mehsoos kiya hua softening/settling hai; neutral joint ki mid-position hai jahan tension kam hoti hai.

question.ur: Pehle vocabulary — clinicians yeh lafz bohat use karte hain. **Point of balance** ka matlab kya hai?

text.en:
So when does **Balanced Ligamentous Tension (BLT)** make sense?
• Gentle treatment of joints or soft tissues in people who cannot tolerate firm techniques.
• Practitioners trained in osteopathic methods.
text.ur: Aise logon mein gentle joint ya soft-tissue treatment ke liye jo firm techniques tolerate nahi karte, aur sirf osteopathic methods mein trained practitioners ke liye. Fracture, instability, infection, unexplained severe pain ya zaroori medical care ko replace karne ke liye use na karein.

text.en:
And just as important — when you should NOT use it, or should stop:
• Fractures, instability, infection or unexplained severe pain.
• Using it to replace needed medical care.
**Stop rule:** Do not use manual stress with suspected fracture, dislocation, major instability, active infection or unexplained neurologic symptoms.
text.ur:
Utna hi zaroori — kab yeh technique NAHI karni, ya kab ruk jana hai:
• Fractures, instability, infection or unexplained severe pain.
• Using it to replace needed medical care.
**Stop rule:** Do not use manual stress with suspected fracture, dislocation, major instability, active infection or unexplained neurologic symptoms.

title.en: How to do it — 6 steps, each with its reason
title.ur: Kaise karein — 6 qadam, har ek ki wajah ke saath

steps.title: Screen and explain
steps.detail: Check for red flags and explain the slow, light technique.

steps.title: Support the joint
steps.detail: For example, support the wrist in the patient's comfortable position.

steps.title: Find balance
steps.detail: Slightly move the joint to find where tension feels even.

steps.title: Hold light contact
steps.detail: Maintain minimal pressure and wait for changes.

steps.title: Release slowly
steps.detail: When the tissue seems to settle, let go gradually.

beats.ur:
1. Red flags screen karke slow, light technique samjhayein.
2. Joint ko support karein, jaise wrist ko comfortable position mein.
3. Halki movement se woh position dhoondhein jahan tension even mehsoos ho.
4. Minimal pressure ke sath hold karke changes ka intezar karein.
5. Tissue settle hota mehsoos ho to ahista release karein.
6. Pain ya movement dobara check karein.

text.en: How much? Typical teaching range: a hold of about 1-5 minutes, light contact only. There is no proven optimum.
text.ur: Teaching mein takreeban 1–5 minute ka light hold bataya jata hai, lekin koi proven optimum duration nahi.

beats.patient: Tom, 62, wrist pain after a fall, fracture excluded, painful with firm touch.
beats.treatment: You hold the wrist in its balanced position with very light contact for three minutes.
beats.reassess: The wrist feels less guarded and rotation is easier. You add gentle exercise.
beats.ur:
Ek misal se poora clinical flow dekhein:
Source mein Tom, 62 saal ke, fall ke baad wrist pain rakhte hain; fracture exclude hai aur firm touch painful hai. Wrist ko halkay contact se balanced position mein 3 minutes hold kiya jata hai. Baad mein guarding kam aur rotation asaan mehsoos hoti hai, phir gentle exercise add hoti hai. Yeh teaching scenario hai.

text.en:
The mistakes I see most often:
• Using force.
• Believing the felt release proves ligament change.
• Ignoring red flags.
**Myth to drop:** 'A tiny position change proves a ligament has been reset.' Comfort and re-measured function are more credible outcomes.
text.ur: Force use karna; mehsoos hone wali release ko ligament change ka proof samajhna; red flags ignore karna. Kya dhoondhna hai? Balanced neutral point. Success kaise judge hogi? Patient-reported pain aur function se.

text.en:
Evidence is minimal. Benefits may come from relaxation and patient context rather than a ligament effect.
Osteopathic texts describe BLT, but high-quality clinical comparisons specific to BLT remain limited; theoretical explanations should not be presented as established tissue corrections.
text.ur: Balance, halka hold, wait aur retest. Evidence minimal hai; faida relaxation aur patient context se aa sakta hai, zaroori nahi ke ligament par specific effect ho.

text.en: One line to carry into the clinic: **Balance, hold lightly, wait, retest.**
